newsitem.title: USA: American Comms seeks to raise capital.
newsitem.headline: American Comms seeks to raise capital.

text.p: American Communications Services Inc said Wednesday that it has begun a private offering of up to $75 million of units to investors that include the company's principal common shareholders.

The company said the proceeds from the sale of the units will be used to fund negative operating cash flow and to pay in full all outstanding ordinary course trade accounts payable that are then more than 60 days overdue to cure a default under its two outstanding public debt issues.
The money will also go toward marketing and product development costs incurred in connection with the company's growth and to expand voice and data networks.
American Communications said it is also soliciting consents from the holders of each of its two outstanding public debt issues for more debt consisting of a new issue of unsecured notes.

If these consents are obtained, the company plans to begin a private debt offering yielding gross proceeds of $125 million to $150 million, which amount will depend on the amount of proceeds raised in the unit offering.
The units consist of redeemable preferred stock due 2008 and warrants to purchase shares common stock.
The exercise price of each warrant will be about 110 percent of the trading price of the ACSI common stock at the time of pricing.
